title: Reading the wizard school's rooms
target: How to use the plates a wizard level hangs on its doors in R.E.P.O., given that the level is a school with named subject rooms and its own hazards.
version: 0.4.0, read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: Enough light to read a plaque
A reason to pick a door

steps.do: Read the plaque before choosing a door.
steps.because: the school signs a dining hall and a lecture hall, with a dungeon below them (Wizard Sign Dining Hall, Wizard Sign Lecture Hall, Wizard Sign Dungeon)

steps.do: Learn the subject rooms, because they are where the level's props live.
steps.because: potions and spells, sorcery, the dark arts and a school of magic plants are each signed (Wizard Sign Potions And Spells, Wizard Sign Sorcery Class, Wizard Sign Dark Arts)

steps.do: Find the administration before you wander.
steps.because: a headmaster's study and a thinking chamber carry plates of their own (Wizard Sign Headmasters Study, Wizard Sign Thinking Chamber)

steps.do: Treat a named hazard as a warning, not scenery.
steps.because: an enchanted lava room, a deathpit corridor and the sludge pits are signed as plainly as the teaching rooms (Wizard Sign Enchanted Lava Room, Wizard Sign Deathpit Corridor, Wizard Sign Sludge Pits of Joy)

steps.do: Check the wings and the courtyard on the way through.
steps.because: a west wing garden, a courtyard and a gnome alley are signed (Wizard Sign West Wing Garden, Wizard Sign Courtyard, Wizard Sign Gnome Alley)

steps.do: Expect blocked and double doors behind the plates.
steps.because: the theme fits its rooms with doors and bookshelves of its own, including blocked and double versions (Wizard Door, Wizard Door Blocked, Wizard Door Double, Wizard Bookshelf Blocked)

commonMistakes: Opening doors at random because the plates all look the same.
Treating the hazard rooms as ordinary corridors.
Assuming the subject rooms hold the same props as the dining hall.
Pushing a blocked door instead of reading the plaque beside it.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; nothing here is estimated.
